A brick the size of my palm was thrown at me,” a student from the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) in Kolkata told Newslaundry on October 4, the day of an incident in which bricks and stones were thrown from outside the college gate. She is one of two female students injured that day. She sustained a head injury that required stitches, while doctors advised the other to undergo a CT scan. The violence was the second flare-up at SRFTI in a week. On September 27, a scuffle broke out between members of the Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat (ABGP), an organisation linked to the RSS, who were attending an event they organised on campus, and SRFTI students protesting against it. A week later, on October 4, a rally associated with the Hindu Jagran Manch, a right-wing Hindu organisation, arrived at the college gate. Students allege that attempts were made to break down the gate and that stone and water bottles were hurled from outside. Following these incidents, students have demanded security from the administration and action against those allegedly responsible for the attacks. They say academic activities at the college will not resume until their demands are met. Two incidents in a week On September 27, the college administration granted the ABGP permission to hold an event on campus. The Student Council opposed this, arguing that college resources should not be used for an event organised by a group associated with a specific political ideology. A clash ensued between students and event attendees during the protest. Students allege that they were assaulted and chased down by the attackers. Several students were injured. Newslaundry has previously reported on this event. Following this incident, on October 4, a poster announcing a march from Ajay Nagar crossing to SRFTI was shared on a Facebook page called ‘Bongiyo Hindu Jagaran Jadavpur District’ of the Hindu Jagran Manch. The post called for the “awakening” of Bengali Hindus. According to Nachiket, a member of the student council, students had learned about the rally two days in advance. He said the students had informed the Vice-Chancellor (VC), police officials, and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. On the day of the rally, students met the V-C to express security concerns, according to Nachiket, but the V-C allegedly said stopping it was beyond his jurisdiction. items.title: Srinagar’s Smart City project is 98% done. But locals say it’s beautification without the basics
items.summary: In the second week of September, a cinema screen floated on the Dal. Srinagar was hosting the first International Film Festival of Jammu and Kashmir, with Chief Minister Omar Abdullah opening it against the Zabarwan hills. It was the city’s biggest international event since the G20 tourism meeting of 2023 and, like that one, mostly an argument made in pictures. Seven weeks earlier, on July 20, an hour of rain had put the same city under water. Lal Chowk, Polo View, Residency Road, the Boulevard, Khanyar, Sada Kadal, Nalamar, Bemina, Dalgate. Water got into the Civil Secretariat, of all places. By evening the valley’s papers had their verdict – so much for the Smart City – and the next day Abdullah called the Secretariat flooding a matter of shame. His cabinet, he said, had already ordered a third-party audit of the Srinagar Smart City project. What the audit will find is anyone’s guess. But what residents describe is fairly consistent. They point to roads raised over drains that still choke, a landfill that keeps growing, a lake that got new decks and cycle tracks but kept its sewage, and beautification in place of the basics. That may be a little unfair to a project that did build some things that work. But it’s hard to argue with people facing these problems, considering that the project is 98 percent finished on paper. Done and dusted? On paper, 157 of 161 sanctioned projects had been completed by March 31, 2026, the Union government told Parliament in July. The completed works cost around Rs 3,530 crore against a sanctioned Rs 3,633 crore. The Smart Cities Mission itself formally ended on March 31, 2025, and the Ministry said no proposal to expand it is under consideration. Four projects are still underway, among them a SCADA-based water management system and water transport on the Jhelum and Dal Lake. Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi had asked in the Lok Sabha whether the government had taken cognisance of the flooding despite the Smart City Mission, and whether the project included storm-water or flood-mitigation works. The Lok Sabha reply named no such project and didn’t explain the flooding. Though drainage was never meant to be optional. The mission’s own guidelines count sanitation and storm-water management among the basics a smart city must deliver. items.title: How a protest for FIR against ACP ended with an FIR against 17 protesters
items.summary: Around 20 people, some of them journalists and content creators, were detained by the Delhi Police on the morning of October 5 from outside the Parliament Street Police Station and taken to the Delhi Police Camp in Delhi Cantonment. They had been sitting outside the police station, protesting against the police for allegedly not registering an FIR against Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat. Bhagat had been promoted as Additional DCP (Deputy Commissioner of Police) before withdrawing from the role “of his own volition” pending a “full enquiry” in the case, according to a government notification . A female journalist has alleged that Bhagat sexually harassed and assaulted her while she was covering the October 2 protest near Jantar Mantar. The police, however, have registered an FIR at the Parliament Street Police Station against 17 of the 20 people detained. Beauty, a friend of the complainant, said at a press conference on October 5, “The police have not filed an FIR on the sexual harassment and assault complaint but have filed an FIR against our people.” The 17 protesters were charged under Sections 223(a), 221, 132, 190 (unlawful assembly), 191(2) (rioting) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), and Section 3 of the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act. According to the police, the protesters violated Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), formed an unlawful assembly, and allegedly attacked police personnel and damaged a bus. On the night of October 5, Patiala House Court granted bail to 17 protesters arrested in connection with the Parliament Street protest. Four were released after furnishing personal bonds, while the remaining 13 were sent to judicial custody as they could not furnish the required sureties. They are to be produced before the concerned court on October 6. The court also noted that two of the accused, Dharmender and Samarth, alleged that they were beaten inside the Parliament Street Police Station after their detention, and their MLCs (medico-legal certificates) recorded injuries. In the bail order, the court noted, “Since the accused, Dharmender and Samarth, have levelled allegations regarding custodial torture, let a report be called from the DCP, New Delhi, regarding the same.” Other detainees and their friends have also alleged that the police beat protesters inside a bus. items.title: एक हफ्ते में दो घटनाएं, एसआरएफटीआई में पढ़ाई रुकी: छात्र बोले- ‘पहले सुरक्षा, फिर क्लास’
items.summary: “मैं कुछ देर पहले ही अस्पताल से वापस आई हूं. मुझ पर मेरी हथेली जितना बड़ा पत्थर फेंका गया था. वो पत्थर नहीं, ईंट थी.” सत्यजीत रे फिल्म एंड टेलीविजन इंस्टीट्यूट (एसआरएफटीआई), कोलकाता की एक छात्रा ने न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री से यह बात उस घटना के अगले दिन बताई, जिसमें उसके मुताबिक कॉलेज गेट के बाहर से पत्थर फेंके गए. वह उन दो छात्राओं में शामिल हैं, जिन्हें 4 अक्टूबर की घटना में चोट लगी. एक छात्रा के सिर में चोट आई, जबकि दूसरी को डॉक्टरों ने सीटी स्कैन कराने की सलाह दी है. पिछले एक हफ्ते में एसआरएफटीआई में दो बार तनाव और झड़प की स्थिति बन चुकी है. 27 सितंबर को कॉलेज कैंपस में आयोजित एक कार्यक्रम के विरोध के दौरान छात्रों और कार्यक्रम में शामिल लोगों के बीच मारपीट हुई थी. इसके ठीक एक हफ्ते बाद, 4 अक्टूबर को हिंदू जागरण मंच से जुड़ी रैली कॉलेज के गेट तक पहुंची. छात्रों का आरोप है कि इस दौरान गेट तोड़ने की कोशिश हुई और बाहर से पत्थर और पानी की बोतलें फेंकी गईं. इन घटनाओं के बाद छात्रों ने प्रशासन से सुरक्षा और हमले के आरोपियों के खिलाफ कार्रवाई की मांग की है. छात्रों का कहना है कि जब तक उनकी मांगें पूरी नहीं होतीं, तब तक कॉलेज में पढ़ाई शुरू नहीं की जाएगी. एक हफ्ते में दो घटनाएं गौरतलब है कि 27 सितंबर को कॉलेज प्रशासन ने आरएसएस से जुड़ी संस्था अखिल भारतीय ग्राहक पंचायत (एबीजीपी) को कैंपस में कार्यक्रम आयोजित करने की अनुमति दी थी. स्टूडेंट काउंसिल ने इसका विरोध किया. छात्रों की आपत्ति थी कि कॉलेज के संसाधनों का इस्तेमाल किसी राजनीतिक विचारधारा से जुड़ी संस्था के कार्यक्रम के लिए नहीं किया जाना चाहिए. विरोध के दौरान छात्रों और कार्यक्रम में शामिल लोगों के बीच झड़प हुई. छात्रों का आरोप है कि उनके साथ मारपीट की गई और उन्हें दौड़ाकर पीटा गया. इस घटना में कई छात्र घायल हुए थे. न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री ने इस घटना पर पहले भी रिपोर्ट की है. इस घटना के बाद 4 अक्टूबर को ‘बोंगियो हिंदी जागरण जादवपुर जिला’ नाम के एक फेसबुक पेज पर अजय नगर चौराहे से एसआरएफटीआई तक मार्च निकालने का पोस्टर साझा किया गया. पोस्ट में बंगाली हिंदुओं को जागृत करने की अपील की गई थी. स्टूडेंट काउंसिल के सदस्य नचिकेत के मुताबिक, छात्रों को इस रैली की जानकारी दो दिन पहले ही मिल गई थी. उन्होंने बताया कि छात्रों ने इसकी जानकारी वाइस चांसलर, पुलिस अधिकारियों और सूचना एवं प्रसारण मंत्रालय को दी थी. नचिकेत के मुताबिक, रैली वाले दिन छात्रों ने वीसी से मुलाकात कर सुरक्षा को लेकर चिंता जताई. उनके अनुसार, वीसी ने कहा कि रैली आएगी और इसे रोकना उनके अधिकार क्षेत्र में नहीं है. नचिकेत का यह भी आरोप है कि छात्रों से उनके नाम सामने आने को लेकर धमकी भरे अंदाज में बात की गई. कॉलेज गेट पर पहुंची भीड़ 4 अक्टूबर को निकली रैली में बड़ी संख्या में लोग शामिल हुए. छात्रों के मुताबिक, कई लोगों के हाथों में भगवा झंडे थे और कुछ के पास डंडे भी थे. छात

items.title: 3 new Supreme Court judges take oath; strength of court rises to 37
items.summary: Three new judges for the Supreme Court of India were administered the oath of office on Tuesday afternoon. The newly appointed judges are Justice Sunita Agarwal (formerly Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court), Justice DK Upadhyay (formerly Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court) and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh (formerly Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court). Justice Sunita Agarwal, Justice DK Upadhyaya, Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh The Central government had notified their appointments as Supreme Court judges on Monday, following a recommendation made by a Supreme Court Collegium on September 28. With their appointments, the top court now has a working strength of 37 judges, just one short of its sanctioned strength of 38 judges. Justice Agarwal, who is originally a judge of the Allahabad High Court, has been the Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court since July 2023. She graduated in law from Awadh University in 1989 and has been in the legal profession since December 1990. She was appointed as a judge in November 2011. She will retire from the Supreme Court in April 2031. Justice Upadhyaya studied law at Lucknow University and enrolled as an advocate in May 1991. He remained the Chief Standing Counsel for the State of Uttar Pradesh from May 2007 till his elevation as a judge in November 2011. In July 2023, he was appointed as the Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court. He was then transferred as the Chief Justice of Delhi High Court in January 2025, in which position he served till his elevation to the Supreme Court. Justice Singh studied law at the University of Delhi and enrolled as an advocate in 1990. He practiced before the Patna High Court from 1990 to 2000 and then before the Jharkhand High Court till elevation as its judge in 2012. He was the Acting Chief Justice of the High Court from December 20, 2022 and February 19, 2023. He was then elevated as the Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court where he took oath on April 17, 2023. Justice Singh was then transferred to the Telangana High Court, where he took oath on July 19, 2025.

items.title: Supreme Court reserves verdict on appeals against removal of mandatory attendance for law students
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday reserved its judgment in a batch of petitions challenging the Delhi High Court ruling that prohibited law colleges from debarring students with attendance shortage from appearing in examinations [ Bar Council of India v. Union of India ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath , Sandeep Mehta and AG Masih reserved its verdict after hearing arguments from the Bar Council of India (BCI), law institutions and others. Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Sandeep Mehta and Justice Augustine George Masih Earlier this year, the top court had stayed the operative direction (paragraph 249) of the High Court judgment prospectively. During those proceedings, the Bench remarked that National Law Universities (NLUs) and colleges across the country were "suffering" as the High Court had "legislated" and effectively given a premium to students lacking discipline. The dispute traces back to a November 2025 judgment of the Delhi High Court. The High Court had initiated a suo motu public interest litigation (PIL) following the 2017 suicide of Amity Law School student Sushant Rohilla, who died after allegedly facing harassment and being forced to repeat an academic year due to low attendance. In that verdict, the High Court held that no student enrolled in a recognised law college or university could be detained from appearing in examinations or progressing academically solely on the ground of insufficient attendance. Challenging the ruling, the BCI and NMIMS Law College argued before the Supreme Court that removing mandatory attendance requirements severely undermines academic rigor, institutional autonomy and professional standards in legal education. It was also highlighted that the High Court order led to a surge in litigation by students seeking examination waivers across multiple institutions. Law students can't be barred from exams for low attendance: Delhi High Court issues guidelines With oral arguments now concluded, the Supreme Court has reserved its judgment. The BCI was represented by Advocate Radhika Gautam. NMIMS was represented by Senior Advocate Mukul Rohatgi along with Advocate Kanu Agrawal.

items.title: Delhi High Court shocked to find one arbitrator handled Axis Bank's 4,155 arbitrations in 5 years
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently expressed shock on finding that one unilaterally appointed sole arbitrator had handled 4,155 arbitral proceedings concerning Axis Bank [ Shikha Ghosh Vs Axis Bank ]. On Court's queries, Axis Bank also disclosed that 76,000 arbitral awards were passed by such sole arbitrators across India in proceedings concerning the bank. A Division Bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Dinesh Bhatt expressed concerns over this state of affairs, terming it the "tip of the iceberg." The Court underscored that such unilateral appointments and repeated appointments of the same arbitrators strike at the neutrality of the arbitral process. "Arbitrators who were appointed in thousands of matters like this without filing proper declarations cannot be said to be independent and impartial arbitrators... handling thousands of the arbitrations by the very same arbitrator appointed by one single party would give rise to justifiable doubts as to independence and impartiality," it said. Justice Prathiba M Singh, Justice Dinesh Bhatt The Court proceeed to order Axis Bank to explain how it permitted the same. "Axis Bank which is the party in the present case is answerable as to how this situation could be permitted and the Bank also requires to take some remedial measures without doubt," the Court said. It also directed the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to caution other banks and financial institutions against unilateral arbitrator appointments. "The RBI being the sector regulator, shall also caution all banks in this regard, so that if any remedial measures need to be taken by other banks and financial institutions in respect of unilateral appointments, the same can also be looked into and some guidance issued in respect thereof," the Court said. The Court was hearing an appeal by one Shikha Ghosh challenging an arbitral award passed in favour of Axis Bank in a loan dispute. The Bank had disbursed a loan of ₹16.66 lakh to Ghosh in 2019 and later initiated arbitration after alleging default in repayment. Ghosh contended that she had not been properly served in the arbitral proceedings and that the award was passed without her knowledge. During the proceedings, the Court asked Axis Bank to disclose, among other things, the number of arbitrations handled by sole arbitrator Vikrant Bhardwaj on behalf of the Bank. items.title: Tried to softly bend laws to ensure justice: Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya bids farewell to Delhi High Court
items.summary: Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya on Tuesday bid farewell to the Delhi High Court, following his recent elevation as a judge of the Supreme Court. Speaking at the full-court farewell reference organised in his honour at the Delhi High Court, Chief Justice (CJ) Upadhyaya underscored that the Chief Justice is merely the “first among equals." CJ Upadhyaya described judging as an effort to bind law, justice, and compassion together. He shared insights into his judicial journey, his approach to justice, and his experience as the Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court. "Like other judges, I came across situations when the law was not able to ensure a just outcome and appeared isolated from justice. In such situations, I tried to softly bend the law towards justice for the deserving litigants. To be able to do so has been a blessing," he said. Reflecting on the debate between "good versus great judges," he went on to remark, "My endeavour has been to be a good judge, may not be a great judge." Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya I came across situations when the law was not able to ensure a just outcome... I tried to softly bend the law towards justice for the deserving litigants. To be able to do so has been a blessing CJ Upadhyaya observed that Delhi is a smaller geographical territory compared to States like Uttar Pradesh or Maharashtra. However, managing the Delhi High Court is far from simple, he pointed out. "The sheer complexity and the cases this court deals with are unparalleled," he said. Drawing an analogy to India's cultural synthesis, he likened the Delhi High Court to an “Indian thali” composed of diverse dishes served together on a single platter. He went on to express deep gratitude for how warmly Delhi embraced him. "India is often described as a melting pot or salad bowl of cultures. Some say India is more like a thali comprising different dishes served on a platter. I agree with them and I find Delhi HC an Indian thali. I am grateful to you for making me feel like home," he said. Concluding his address on a lighter note, CJ Upadhyaya quoted Oscar Wilde and said, “Some cause happiness wherever they go; others whenever they go. I don't know in which category I will be placed, but the answer lies with posterity.” The gathering included fellow High Court judges, Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, and other members of the Bar. items.title: Kerala High Court sets aside preventive detention of BJP councillor R Suguthan under KAAPA
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday set aside the preventive detention order passed under the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (KAAPA), 2007, against Thiruvananthapuram Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) councillor Sugathan R [Aswathi GR v State of Kerala & ors]. Justices Anil K Narendran and Muralee Krishna S delivered the judgment on a petition filed by Sugathan's wife, Aswathi GR challenging the detention order passed against him on June 8. " Writ petition is allowed. Registry shall communicate the order to the 4th Respondent (Superintendent, Central Prison & Correctional Home, Viyyur, Thrissur), " the Court said. JUSTICE ANIL K NARENDRAN AND JUSTICE MURALEE KRISHNA S Suguthan is a BJP councillor from Ward Number 20 of the Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation. He was placed under preventive detention by an order passed by the District Magistrate, Thiruvananthapuram. He was subsequently detained on June 9 and lodged at the Viyyur Central Prison. The State government later confirmed his detention by an order dated July 6 based on the opinion of the KAAPA Advisory Board. His wife then approached the High Court contending that the detention was illegal and alleged that Sugathan's detention had not been properly communicated to him. She alleged that several pages of the documents relied upon for his detention were either missing or illegible, preventing Sugathan from effectively challenging his detention. She also stated that relevant materials concerning the criminal cases against him had not been considered by the detaining authority. The detention authority had taken into account seven criminal cases registered against Sugathan at Vattiyoorkavu Police Station between 2019 and 2026. Six had been chargesheeted and were pending trial, while one case registered in 2026 was under investigation. She disputed the circumstances surrounding several of these cases and stated that some arose due to counter-cases while one stemmed from a political protest. Earlier, Suguthan had approached the Court in a different proceeding after he was unable to take his oath as a councillor because of his detention. The Court had permitted Suguthan to take the oath inside the prison while observing that the mandate of the electorate could not be defeated merely because an elected representative was under preventive detention. items.title: Law clerk experience cannot be equated with bench clerk's for judicial service eligibility: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday observed that the experience gained by a law clerk cannot be equated with that of a bench clerk for the purpose of fulfilling the eligibility requirement of prior legal practice to take the judicial service examinations [ Tapasmita Sutar vs Union of India ]. A law clerk is a law graduate engaged for a fixed term to help a judge with research and drafting, while a bench clerk is a court staff member who manages courtroom administration, such as calling cases, handling files and recording orders dictated by a judge. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi , and Justice V Mohana today observed that the two roles cannot be equated while determining a person's eligibility to take the judicial services exam. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana The Court was hearing a petition moved by a judicial services aspirant who had served as a bench clerk in the district judiciary. The petitioner, who had previously appeared in the 2023 judicial service examination, approached the top court contending that her employment in the subordinate judiciary barred her from active practice at the Bar. She consequently sought parity with judicial law clerks, whose clerkship period is counted towards the mimimum bar/ legal practice experience to write the entry-level judicial services exam. The petitioner requested that her service as a bench clerk be similarly counted towards the mandatory practice threshold. The Bench, however, rejected this claim of parity, holding that there is a reasonable classification between research-focused law clerks and ministerial staff. " There is a clear rational nexus in a law clerk's experience being utilised as equivalent to practice, which cannot be conflated and extended to other ministerial staff assisting a court ," Justice Bagchi observed. Supreme Court Law clerks have a unique role to play and cannot be equated with bench clerks... There is a clear rational nexus in a law clerk's experience being utilised as equivalent to practice The petitioner's counsel had submitted that she was placed at an unfair disadvantage as her employment prevented her from entering active practice. items.title: BITS Law School commences admissions for 2027-28
items.summary: BITS Law School, Mumbai, a Law School under the aegis of BITS Pilani, an Institution of Eminence, invites applications for its five-year integrated, fully residential law programmes for the 2027 intake. The admissions process has commenced for its B.A. LL.B. (Hons) and B.B.A. LL.B. (Hons). These programmes, approved by the Bar Council of India, combine core legal education with interdisciplinary learning across areas relevant to contemporary legal practice. Students can choose from the five specialisations : Technology & Media Law, Corporate & Financial Law, Entertainment & Sports Law, Alternative Dispute Resolution & Mediation, and Public Law & Theory. The admissions process follows the BITS Law Foundation Assessment (BLFA), a holistic approach that takes into consideration academic performance, recognised law entrance examination scores, extracurricular achievements, communication skills, and personal interview performance. It seeks to understand the individual behind the score, including the student’s ability to comprehend, communicate, reason, articulate ideas, and engage with contemporary issues. Through structured interactions with faculty, applicants get an opportunity to demonstrate their intellectual curiosity, analytical thinking, communication skills, and motivation to study law. This approach reflects the School’s belief that potential for legal education cannot always be captured by a single examination score, but requires an admission process that assesses not just what a student knows, but how they think and communicate. Every year, around 7,000 applicants apply for the five-year integrated law programmes. Candidates applying for the law programmes must have secured a minimum of 45% in Grade 12. Students awaiting their Class 12 or entrance examination results may also apply, with admission subject to submission of their final scores. Candidates can apply through the BITS LAT (BITS Law Entrance Test) or with scores from recognised law entrance examinations, including CLAT, AILET, SLAT, MHCET Law, and LNAT . items.title: Karnataka High Court questions ED’s belated FEMA proceedings against Cafe Coffee Day CEO Malavika Hegde
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday took exception to the Enforcement Directorate (ED) initiating proceedings under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA) against Cafe Coffee Day CEO Malavika Hegde after a delay of more that 12 years in connection with a 2010 transaction. Justice KS Hemalekha asked ED whether proceedings could be initiated after such a long lapse of time. “You cannot do something after so many years,” the Court orally observed. Hegde is the widow of late VG Siddhartha, the founder of Cafe Coffee Day. The Court was hearing he petition challenging the show-cause notice and subsequent hearing notices issued by the FEMA adjudicating authority. Justice K S Hemalekha The High Court had earlier, on January 19, stayed the proceedings initiated by the ED under FEMA against Malavika Hegde . During the hearing on Tuesday, the Court questioned the applicability of Section 43 of FEMA, which deals with the continuation of certain rights and obligations arising under Section 13 even after the death or insolvency of the person liable. The Court observed that while Section 43 provides for the devolution of certain rights and obligations upon legal representatives, the issue was whether such proceedings could be initiated after an unreasonable period of time. “What is reasonable is reasonable for all acts. It was argued that Section 43 of FEMA enables the authorities to proceed against the legal heirs in respect of liabilities arising from the transactions. items.title: The Indian arbitration hub that runs like a members' club
items.summary: William Shakespeare famously said, “all the world’s a stage, and all the men and women merely players.” What he perhaps forgot to tell us is who gets to decide the cast. The lights are bright enough to make even the oldest suits look new. The dialogues have been rehearsed. The exotic dishes are already on the table. The logistics have been taken care of. Everyone knows where to sit, when to smile and, more importantly, whom to speak to. There is a corner of the room sit My Lords (retired) who once occupied the highest chairs of the judiciary, whose names still carry the weight of the offices they once held. They converse casually with those who may, in time, hold the baton themselves. There is laughter, there are handshakes and there is the familiar exchange of courtesies that accompanies gatherings of this kind. The night, however, is going to be long. The deal is not. It is remarkably short and surprisingly simple. My Lords (retired) have already been told what part they are expected to perform. The designated seniors, meanwhile, have already been given their script to be read before My Lord (retired) by the script writer. If enthusiasm could be converted into infrastructure, India would already be running the world's arbitration hub out of a single, endlessly reused conference hall somewhere between Geneva and Singapore, complete with a standing power point template, a rotating cast of keynote speakers and a buffet that has, by now, probably earned its own citation in legal literature. 30 years after the promise was made in 1996, India still seems better at talking about becoming an arbitration hub than actually becoming one. The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is at an age where a statute deserves to be judged less by the conferences organised in its honour and more by the ecosystem that has actually grown beneath it. India has, to its credit, built a sophisticated self-appointed arbitration bar and a growing institutional infrastructure, but somewhere along the way, the ambition of building an arbitration hub appears to have been quietly swapped for the comfort of maintaining an arbitration club. And the two are not the same thing at all. A hub should welcome anyone who has the ability to enter, while a club remains limited to those whom someone chooses to let in. Justice Sibo Sankar Mishra held that the protection under Section 32A of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) prevented civil or criminal liability for acts attributable to the earlier management from being fastened on Tata Steel, after the resolution plan resulted in a change in management and control. “ Any civil or criminal liability arising from acts or omissions attributable to the erstwhile BSL cannot be fastened upon the present petitioner-company (Tata Steel) ,” the Court said. items.title: Plea before Supreme Court over failure to fill vacancies in State Human Rights Commissions
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday sought responses from the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), the Central government and various States on a plea alleging that several State Human Rights Commissions (SHRCs) remain vacant, understaffed or defunct [ Association of Retired Judges of Supreme Court and High Courts of India v NHRC and Ors. ]. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana issued notice on the petition filed by the Association of Retired Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts of India. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The petition before the Court seeks directions to the Union and State governments to ensure that the SHRCs are properly staffed and are able to function under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 (which provides for bodies to inquire into complaints of human-rights violations). The petitioners relied on the 2015 Supreme Court judgment in DK Basu v. State of West Bengal , in which the Court held that filling vacancies in SHRCs was not merely an option for governments but a duty. In that judgment, the Court had directed governments to fill existing vacancies of Chairpersons and Members within three months. Additionally, it had also order all future vacancies to be filled within three months of them arising. "More than a decade has elapsed since those directions, yet the default persists across the country," states the petition. According to the plea, several States continue to have vacant posts of Chairpersons and Members, while some SHRCs have allegedly remained non-functional for prolonged periods. The petitioners' analysis of the 28 State commissions claims that 10 States do not have a permanent Chairperson, 3 SHRCs are defunct, 7 do not have a judicial Member, and 16 do not have a non-judicial Member. The plea also alleges that 23 States have not made their SHRCs' annual reports available online. Under the 1993 law, these reports are meant to record the commissions' work and be placed before the respective State legislatures. The petition says only 5 States, Goa, Maharashtra, Punjab, Sikkim and Uttarakhand, had annual reports publicly available. The petition further raises concerns over a shortage of administrative and investigative staff in the SHRCs. It relies on Section 27 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, which requires State governments to provide the commissions with necessary officers, police and other staff.

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday urged the Delhi Police not to hesitate in taking strict action against 'goons' found threatening the safety of women in Delhi, and to instil genuine fear in the minds of those who intend to commit crimes against women. A Bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran underscored that policing cannot remain confined to files and orders on paper, but must translate into visible deterrence on the streets. "We are in a country like India. Merely putting things on paper is not enough. You need to get into action. If you have to be a little more strict, a little more harsh, do not hesitate. The Court noted that the goal must be crime prevention rather than action after the crime has occurred. "There should be a fear, a fright in the mind of the man who is prone to commit such offences. Unless that fear and fright is created ki ‘ab kuch kiya toh marr jayenge’ (if we do anything now, we will be finished), you will not be able to prevent such crimes. items.title: Gujarat High Court Advocates' Association to abstain from court work for 2 days over Gujarat Rent Bill 2026
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court Advocates' Association (GHCAA) on Monday resolved to abstain from court work on October 5 and 6 in solidarity with lawyers protesting provisions of the Gujarat Rent Bill, 2026. The decision was taken at an Extraordinary General Body meeting held at Gate No. 2 of the Gujarat High Court on Monday morning. The meeting was chaired by the GHCAA President, Senior Advocate Yatin Oza . The GHCAA said the decision was taken in support of lawyers practising before the City Civil Court and Small Causes Court and in line with a resolution passed by the Bar Council of Gujarat (BCG). The protest arose over certain provisions of the Gujarat Rent Bill, 2026, which seeks to shift the adjudication of rent-related disputes from courts to revenue authorities. The Bill has been passed by the Gujarat Legislative Assembly and is currently awaiting the Governor's approval. The Bill provides for authorities, including Deputy Collectors and Additional Collectors, to hear and decide such disputes. Lawyers across Ahmedabad had began protesting against the proposal last week. Notably, advocates at the City Civil and Small Causes Courts had abstained from work and blocked access to the Bhadra court complex as part of the protest. The BCG subsequently convened an extraordinary general body meeting on October 3 and extended its support to the protest. It resolved that lawyers across Gujarat would abstain from proceedings before courts, tribunals, judicial and quasi-judicial authorities and revenue forums from October 5 until a satisfactory resolution of the issue. Additionally, the BCG's resolution said the transfer of the power to decide rent disputes from judicial to administrative authorities would affect lawyers, litigants and the public. It also expressed concerns over the workload of administrative officials and the process of recording and evaluating evidence in rent disputes. BCG Chairman PD Patel told The Times of India that the government had transferred rent-dispute adjudication from the judiciary to what he described as an already overburdened bureaucracy. The Council has sought a meeting with Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel and Law Minister to press for amendments to the Bill to restore the power to decide rent disputes to judicial authorities. The GHCAA said its two-day work abstention was intended to show solidarity with lawyers practising before the City Civil Court and Small Causes Court amid the ongoing protest against the Bill. items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday dismissed a batch of petitions seeking action against politicians for hate speech that allegedly led to the North-East Delhi riots of 2020. A Division Bench of Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain also dismissed a batch of petitions seeking an inquiry by a Special Investigation Team (SIT) into alleged police atrocities that took place in Jamia Millia Islamia in 2019 during a march against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA). items.title: BRS leader Manne Krishank arrested over allegations against CM Revanth Reddy’s daughter
items.summary: Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) leader Manne Krishank was arrested by the Hyderabad Cyber Crimes police on Tuesday, October 6, over allegations he made against Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy’s daughter, Naimisha Reddy, regarding the ownership of pharmaceutical companies. Krishank was booked under Sections 353(2) (statements conducing to public mischief) and 352 (intentional insult) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), following a complaint by Congress leader Mettu Sai Kumar. The complaint alleged that Krishank had made false and defamatory statements about Naimisha’s alleged links to certain properties and pharmaceutical companies. The arrest comes amid an escalating political confrontation between the ruling Congress and the opposition BRS over the business interests and assets of Revanth Reddy’s family. Three days before his arrest, on October 3, Krishank had held a press conference at the BRS headquarters in Hyderabad and demanded an Enforcement Directorate (ED) probe into the alleged business interests, assets, investments and financial transactions of Revanth Reddy and his family members. Krishank alleged that companies including Maxbien Pharma, Medicover Hospitals, Sahrudaya Healthcare and Geetha Automotive had links with members of the Chief Minister’s family. He questioned their ownership structures, shareholdings, beneficial ownership and financial transactions, and called for an independent investigation. He also alleged that the family’s assets and business interests had grown substantially in recent years and claimed they were worth more than Rs 50,000 crore. Krishank further alleged that Rs 13,000 crore in unaccounted money had been converted into legitimate funds through transactions involving Medicover. Krishank has previously raised questions about Maxbien Pharma. Three days ago, he alleged that Naimisha’s husband, Annam Sarath, her father-in-law, Satyanarayana Reddy Golugiri, and Dumpa Sirisha were directors of the company. He alleged that the company had benefited from government favours and made substantial profits. The BRS leader has also questioned alleged business links involving Medicover Hospitals and other companies. He called for scrutiny of their ownership and financial structures and said that the party would submit documents and company records to investigating agencies.

items.title: TN opposition parties slam police action against nurses' protest in Chennai
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Hundreds of Mid-Level Healthcare providers (MHLP) protesting in Chennai over demands including permanent employment and equal pay for equal work were detained by the police, prompting sharp criticism from opposition leaders. The protest was later temporarily deferred until November 3, following talks between the government and nurses’ representatives. Members of the Tamil Nadu Mid-Level Healthcare Providers’ Union staged a hunger strike near Rajarathinam Stadium in Egmore on Monday, October 5, with more than 500 nurses participating and raising slogans demanding that the government address their grievances. The MLHPs, who work at Health and Wellness Centres across Tamil Nadu, are seeking permanent employment, job security, equal pay for equal work and a monthly salary of Rs 45,000. The union has also demanded payment of pending incentives for 2023 and 2024, paid maternity leave, medical leave, higher incentives for services provided at wellness centres and promotional opportunities. It has sought to redesignate MLHPs as Community Health Officers (CHOs), along with certificates recognising the designation. According to the union, 4,848 MLHPs are currently working on a contractual basis across the state. Recruited in 2021, they provide services including antenatal care, immunisation, emergency referrals, adolescent care, family welfare, outpatient care, non-communicable disease management, and activities under the National Health Mission. Union president N Sundari said MLHPs were paid Rs 21,000 in Tamil Nadu despite doing a range of healthcare work. She said salaries and incentives for similar workers were higher in several other states. items.title: After journo alleges sexual assault by Delhi ACP, those demanding FIR booked
items.summary: Around 20 people, some of them journalists and content creators, were detained by the Delhi Police on the morning of October 5 from outside the Parliament Street Police Station and taken to the Delhi Police Camp in Delhi Cantonment. They had been sitting outside the police station, protesting against the police for allegedly not registering an FIR against Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat. Bhagat had been promoted as Additional DCP (Deputy Commissioner of Police) before withdrawing from the role “of his own volition” pending a “full enquiry” in the case, according to a government notification . A female journalist has alleged that Bhagat sexually harassed and assaulted her while she was covering the October 2 protest near Jantar Mantar. The police, however, have registered an FIR at the Parliament Street Police Station against 17 of the 20 people detained. Beauty, a friend of the complainant, said at a press conference on October 5, “The police have not filed an FIR on the sexual harassment and assault complaint but have filed an FIR against our people.” The 17 protesters were charged under Sections 223(a), 221, 132, 190 (unlawful assembly), 191(2) (rioting) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), and Section 3 of the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act. According to the police, the protesters violated Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), formed an unlawful assembly, and allegedly attacked police personnel and damaged a bus. On the night of October 5, Patiala House Court granted bail to 17 protesters arrested in connection with the Parliament Street protest. Four were released after furnishing personal bonds, while the remaining 13 were sent to judicial custody as they could not furnish the required sureties. They are to be produced before the concerned court on October 6. The court also noted that two of the accused, Dharmender and Samarth, alleged that they were beaten inside the Parliament Street Police Station after their detention, and their MLCs (medico-legal certificates) recorded injuries. In the bail order, the court noted, “Since the accused, Dharmender and Samarth, have levelled allegations regarding custodial torture, let a report be called from the DCP, New Delhi, regarding the same.” Other detainees and their friends have also alleged that the police beat protesters inside a bus. items.summary: Following allegations of religious discrimination in the employment of security guards for dandiya events during Navratri in Hyderabad, All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) Asaduddin Owaisi called on the police to take strict action against such occurrences. Earlier on October 4, a group of Hindu and Muslim individuals working as bouncers in Hyderabad addressed the media and alleged that they had been facing discrimination from organisers of dandiya events since 2024. Mohammed Feroz (Fazal), a bouncer, alleged that event organisers have been saying they were under pressure not to employ Muslims. “If that’s the case, the organisers must complain to the police about those who are promoting religious discrimination. We request the police to act against such people,” he said. Fazal also alleged that while the discrimination began at dandiya events two years ago, it has since crept into hiring of security guards in clubs and hotels as well. A few of Fazal’s Hindu colleagues who were present also asked event organisers not to discriminate against an entire community. They said that Hindus and Muslims want to coexist peacefully in Telangana but some groups were trying to stoke communal tension through religious discrimination. “Muslim bouncers and other workers have reported that event organisers are boycotting them under pressure from extremist organisations. This poison can be curbed if the police take strict action. More importantly, the people of Telangana must stand united across religions against this evil. Otherwise, the state’s progress and development will also become a victim,” Hyderabad MP Owaisi said.
